summary: This resolution designates the House Press Gallery rooms (H–315 through H–319) in the U.S. Capitol as the Frederick Douglass Press Gallery.

scores.thoughts: The bill is a purely symbolic resolution renaming a press gallery. It contains no provisions related to federal budgets, appropriations, or expenditures of any kind.
The bill makes no reference to tax policy, rates, credits, or revenue measures.
No content in the resolution addresses healthcare systems, coverage, or policy.
The resolution has zero connection to firearms regulation or Second Amendment issues.
Nothing in the bill pertains to immigration, borders, or related legal pathways.
The bill does not engage with reproductive rights or abortion policy.
No provisions or implications regarding military or defense spending appear in the text.
The resolution contains no environmental or regulatory language.
No references to welfare programs, entitlements, or social services.
The bill is unrelated to schools, funding, or education policy.
No mention of drugs, enforcement, or decriminalization.
The resolution does not address sentencing, policing, or justice reform.
Zero connection to tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization.
The bill has no bearing on deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
No provisions related to LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
The resolution does not address foreign assistance or international aid.
No content concerning voting access, election integrity, or electoral procedures.
The bill contains nothing about technology regulation or data privacy.
No references to workers' rights, unions, or employment policy.
While the honoree advocated for civil rights, the bill itself is a ceremonial naming with no policy provisions on religious liberty or anti-discrimination law.
